safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Increase SAP safety lead time from 0.0 to 1.4 days

narrative: Material PL3__MBAA96BA shows very smooth daily demand (CV=0.029) averaging 45,851 units per working day with no detectable trend across the observation period. However, lead times exhibit moderate-to-high variability (CV=0.821, range 0.1–5.0 days), which dominates the safety stock requirement. An (r,Q) policy is chosen because demand is continuous and smooth, making fixed-order-quantity replenishment efficient. The EOQ of 122,558 units exceeds the MOQ of 83,078 and remains within the storage capacity constraint.
warnings: Current SAP safety stock is 0 — inadequate for 95% service level given lead time variability
Lead time CV=0.821 is high; transport variability is the dominant risk factor

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth (CV=0.029) and nearly continuous (97.3% non-zero days), making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal. The EOQ formula minimises total holding and ordering costs; the reorder point absorbs lead time uncertainty via the safety stock buffer.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding (safety_stock + order_quantity = 219,528 < 349,999). No capacity-driven service degradation is anticipated.
